The fraud was identified by tracing card usage through transactions, devices, and cards in TigerGraph. The affected cards and the cardholder were monitored, and the card was blocked.

sar.narrative: Customer C04274, holder of card C04274-K1, is the subject of this suspicious activity report. Between 2016-11-18 19:12 and 2016-11-28 15:34, 3 transactions totaling $484.76 were made online on the card using handset device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' routed through an anonymous proxy. The specific transactions consisted of $144.21 on 2016-11-18 19:12 (transaction 3468463), $221.02 on 2016-11-21 17:34 (transaction 3476202), and $119.53 on 2016-11-28 15:34 (transaction 3494535). The activity is suspicious because the same device profile was used across 28 cards in a 60-day window around the alert, all 28 behind an anonymous proxy and flagged as new devices, pointing to organized cyber-enabled fraud infrastructure. Furthermore, 4 closed cases on cards using this profile were confirmed fraud with an undocumented pattern, and 8 of the 8 most similar closed cases (including CC-2985, CC-2649, CC-0849, and CC-3035) were confirmed fraud. For the final session involving the $119.53 purchase, the one-time passcode sent to the cardholder's registered phone was not completed. When contacted separately, the cardholder stated they did not make the transactions and still physicaly holds card C04274-K1. In response to these findings, the bank has recommended blocking card C04274-K1 (L1), automatically created a case, monitored connected cards, filed this report (L2), and escalated the matter to an analyst.
